column2: Retain Naaman's Syrian command, esteem before his master, the Lord's deliverance of Syria through him and his strength alongside leprosy. Divine deliverance is explicitly given to Syria here; the disease label is not a precise modern medical diagnosis.

Retain the lightly equipped Syrians, captive young girl from Israel and service to Naaman's wife. Lightly equipped interprets monozonoi, literally singly girded, without specifying weapons or denying the coercion of captivity.

Retain the girl's wish that her master stand before God's prophet in Samaria and the expectation of release from leprosy. Mistress and master are human referents; the prophet is not yet named in this speech.

Retain She and her own master because the selected reflexive is feminine. The account reports what the Israelite girl said; it is not silently replaced with Naaman reporting to the king. The exact female reporter remains unresolved.
column3: Does the feminine reflexive identify Naaman's wife, the girl or another inherited subject transition; should the English retain She until that is settled?

column2: Retain the Syrian king's instruction, promised letter and Naaman's ten silver talents, six thousand gold coins and ten robe changes. Gold coins is an inherited interpretation of substantival chrysous, not evidence of a separately named denomination.
column3: Should gold pieces replace gold coins to avoid overdefining the form of the selected gold payment?

column2: Retain the letter's arrival formula, Behold, Naaman as the sender's slave and the directive that the recipient free him from leprosy. It said makes the letter the natural English speaker without pretending that a separate saying verb has a new named author.

Retain torn garments, the negative God question, killing/making alive and the perceived pretext against the king. The final understand/see appeal represents his interpretation of the request; no narrator confirmation of Syrian hostile intent is added.

Retain Elisha's hearing, message to Israel's king, question about torn garments and named invitation for Naaman to know there is a prophet in Israel. The response does not promise that the king personally will perform healing.
Retain a horse and chariot and the doors of Elisha's house. The selected equipment is singular in form; no retinue's exact size is supplied from the later whole-company statement.

Retain the messenger as intermediary, seven baths in the Jordan, restored flesh and cleansing. The instruction is not softened to a general washing, and the future result remains distinct from the command.

Retain Naaman's anger, departure, presentative and expected sequence: emergence, standing, invocation, hand placed on the place and removal of the leprous condition. The selected hand action is not changed to waving over the area.

Retain Abanah and Pharpar, Damascus, comparison with both Jordan and all Israel's waters, the bathing/cleansing question and angry withdrawal. The comparison remains Naaman's objection, not an editorial geographic assessment.

Retain the positive great-thing statement, the question will you not do it and the quoted command. The selected speech does not say if the prophet had asked a difficult thing, and no Father address or explicit how much more clause is imported.
column3: How should the final kai hoti connect the washing command to the great-word assertion without replacing the selected syntax with the familiar counterfactual argument?

column2: Retain Naaman going down, dipping seven times, Elisha's word and restored flesh like a little child's. The repeated and rhythm remains acceptable narrative sequencing; no additional ritual interpretation of baptizo is supplied.

Retain return with the whole company, standing, Behold, recognition of God only in Israel and the requested acceptance of a blessing. Blessing here denotes the offered gift in context without erasing its chosen term or expanding the theological statement.

Retain Elisha's oath by the Lord before whom he stands and refusal to accept despite pressure. I will not accept expresses the negative force of the elliptical if oath; the two actors' pronouns remain contextually distinct.

Retain the conditional response, pair-of-mules load, explicit red earth and promise of offerings to the Lord alone. Earth is not generalized into a symbolic gift, and the selected doubled request, be given/you shall give, remains.

Retain the future Lord will be propitious twice and all three Remman-house references. The master's bowing, support on Naaman's arm and Naaman's own bowing remain distinct. The statement is not silently converted into a past deed or an explicit editorial permission to worship.
column3: Do the future propitiation verbs express assurance or a petition in this speech, and how should the repeated bowing clauses be punctuated to keep their subjects clear?

column2: Retain Go in peace as the idiomatic dismissal and debratha of the land as an unresolved distance expression. Debratha is not converted into a measured distance or confidently treated as a place-name.
column3: What distance or idiomatic range does debratha represent, and can it be translated without importing another text's wording?

column2: Retain Gehazi's presentative, his complaint that the master spared this Syrian, the withheld gift and his oath to pursue and take something. The affirmative force of if not in the oath is rendered I will; no justification of his action is added.
Retain Gehazi pursuing, Naaman seeing the runner and turning back from the chariot to meet him. The text does not explicitly narrate a full dismount, so that action is not supplied.

Retain Peace and Gehazi's claimed message about two prophetic young men from Ephraim, one talent and two robe changes. The claim remains attributed speech; no additional peace question by Naaman is imported into the preceding unit.

Retain the offer of two talents, two bags, two robe changes and two attendants carrying ahead. The unexpressed subject of took and the final him remain contextually inferred rather than newly named; no extra urging clause is supplied.
column3: Who takes and packages the silver in the selected verb sequence, and does the final ahead of him refer to Gehazi?

column2: Retain the dark place, taking goods from their hands, storing in a house and dismissal. Goods supplies the implied object. Dark place is not replaced with a named hill or tower without a source decision.
column3: Is to skoteinon a dark location, an architectural place or a transliterated/topographic expression in this context?

column2: Retain Gehazi's entry and standing by his master, the elliptical From where question and denial of going here or there. The lie is allowed to emerge from the narrative rather than receiving an added moral label in the verse.

Retain the heart-going question, chariot encounter, both now-you-have-taken clauses and future acquisition list. Gardens, olives, vineyards, sheep, cattle and male/female servants all remain. This is not recast as the familiar is this a time to receive question.

Retain Naaman's leprosy clinging to Gehazi and offspring for ever, then the snow comparison at departure. The image is not expanded into a precise clinical description or a claim about a modern hereditary mechanism.

Retain the prophetic sons' presentative and complaint that the dwelling before Elisha is too narrow. Before you preserves their relation to the prophet without inventing an institution's physical layout.

Retain the Jordan destination, one beam per man, communal building and repeated there. The unexpressed building object is left implicit; the prophet's deute is naturally read as permission Go on in the following sequence.
Retain one person's polite invitation to accompany your slaves and Elisha's affirmative I will go. The request does not take divine-address forms, and no individual name is supplied.
Retain Elisha's going with them, arrival at Jordan and timber-cutting. The plural laborers remain distinct from the following individual whose iron falls.

Retain Behold, the individual bringing down a beam, iron falling into water and the borrowed-item cry to the human lord. Iron is not expanded into an elaborate tool description; the borrowed status follows kechremenon provisionally.
column3: Does kechremenon mean borrowed here or more generally being used, and can the beam-felling scene establish axe head without overtranslation?

column2: Retain the location question and indication, chipping wood, throwing it there and the iron floating. The selected narrative does not give a physical mechanism, and no replacement handle or river depth is added.
Retain the instruction to lift it for himself and the outstretched hand taking it. The two he subjects are understood from speaker and recipient; no different retriever is introduced.

Retain the Syrian king's war and consultation, the particular camp location and inherited Elmoni. Elmoni remains an unresolved expression, not an approved geographic identification; capitalization should not settle its status.
column3: Does elmoni function as an indefinite such-and-such expression rather than a place-name, and how should the combined location wording be rendered?

column2: Retain Elisha's warning against passing through that place because Syria is concealed there. The danger is an ambush-like concealment; no battle already fought at the location is invented.

Retain the king sending to the indicated place, guarding himself from there and not once or twice. The exact relation of reconnaissance, location and personal protection is elliptical; no third occurrence count is inferred from the idiom.
column3: How should ephylaxato ekeithen be expressed naturally while preserving the location relation and leaving the unexpressed object of sent open?

column2: Retain the Syrian king's shaken soul and question about betrayal to Israel's king. The emotion is represented without diagnosing it; the suspected informant remains unnamed.

Retain the attendant's denial, human my lord king and Elisha's reporting of all bedroom words. The chamber-of-bedroom expression is selected and is not expanded into a claim about how the prophet acquires the knowledge.

Retain the command to locate Elisha, intended sending and seizure, and the presentative Dothaim report. The named location is not silently standardized to another place spelling without the name register's review.
Retain horse and chariot forces, a heavy/large force, night arrival and encirclement. The English collective forces expresses singular equipment nouns without inventing troop numbers.

Propose and behold, an army was encircling for and there was an army encircling to retain the selected presentative. The minister's early rising, horse/chariot forces and alarmed What shall we do remain unchanged.
Retain the prohibition of fear and comparison that those with us exceed those with them. The unseen allies are not named as angels in this sentence, and the plural us includes prophet and attendant.

Retain the prayer, opened eyes, Behold, mountain full of horses and singular chariot of fire around Elisha. The inherited prayer has no second-person pronoun needing Thou; no plural fiery chariots or claim that every horse is fiery is supplied.

Retain the attackers' descent, direct prayer I pray Thee, this nation, blindness and the Lord's action according to Elisha's word. I pray Thee is an English petition marker for the Greek request particle, not a claim that an explicit second-person object occurs.
column3: What kind of impaired sight does aorasia denote here, given the group's subsequent ability to follow Elisha?

column2: Retain the negative city/road declaration, follow-me command and promise to lead them to the man sought, then arrival in Samaria. The single Greek negation is interpreted as covering both coordinated nouns; the ethical or tactical explanation is not inserted.
column3: Does the negation cover both city and road as rendered, and how should the deictic statement be understood in the immediate setting?

column2: Retain entry into Samaria, the direct prayer using Thee, opened eyes, sight and the presentative discovery in the middle of Samaria. The petition marker remains an idiomatic expansion; the divine/human referents are not confused.

Retain the king's seeing and emphatic strike question to the human father, Elisha. Indeed represents the repeated striking construction without adding a separate second command or changing strike to a guaranteed kill.

Retain the negative strike instruction with the difficult exception concerning sword/bow captives, then food, water and release. The selected ei me clause is not silently rewritten as a rhetorical question that denies killing all captives; its scope remains open.
column3: How do the prohibition, ei me exception and present you strike fit together; is another punctuation or interrogative reading warranted?

column2: Retain the great spread, eating/drinking, dismissal and return to their master. The cessation applies to Syria's lightly equipped troops; the following royal siege is not erased to harmonize the notices.

Retain after this, the son of Ader as Syria's king, his whole force and siege of Samaria. The transition is preserved without supplying an elapsed time or declaring that the previous cessation was permanent in every sense.

Propose Behold before they besieged to restore the selected presentative. The famine, fifty-shekel donkey head and five-shekel quarter-kab of pigeon dung remain. Fifty is not replaced by eighty, and dung is not confidently reidentified as a plant.
column3: Does pigeon dung refer literally to excrement or an idiomatic commodity here; the selected price and measure should remain pending that decision.

column2: Retain the king passing along the wall and the woman's plea Save me, lord king. Me supplies the natural object of the rescue command; lord is human address and does not require Thee.

Retain the negative wish May the Lord not save you from Greek mē with the optative, followed by the king's question about saving from threshing floor or winepress. It is not silently converted into if the Lord does not help, despite the difficulty of the curse-like wording.
column3: Is the selected negative optative best read as a wish, an elliptical protest or another idiom; retain the provisional wording until that syntax is resolved.

column2: Retain the king's inquiry and the woman's report of the proposed two-day exchange of sons for eating. The speech remains attributed and its explicit violence is neither embellished nor euphemized; the second son is tied to tomorrow.
Retain boiling and eating her son, the next day's demand for the other's son and the hiding. The report does not say that the second child was also killed; the contrast explains the complaint.

Retain the king's hearing, torn garments, continued movement on the wall and the people's sight of sackcloth against his flesh underneath. The inner garment is not made into a newly adopted act after the complaint.
Retain the self-imprecating God oath and the condition concerning Elisha's head remaining that day. The negative intention emerges from the oath rather than an added explicit execution order here.

Retain Elisha with the elders, the king as the contextual sender, warning about the son of a murderer, shutting/pressing at the door and the master's footsteps behind. The king and Elisha names clarify unexpressed subjects from the narrative; the precise door restraint remains provisional.
column3: Does press him at the door mean restrain the messenger or hold the door shut against him, and how securely is the following master identified as the king?

column2: Retain both presentatives, the messenger descending during the speech and the calamity-from-the-Lord question about waiting. The selected messenger is not replaced with king; the actual speaker may be reporting the master's message, which remains unresolved.
column3: Who voices the final complaint, the messenger directly or the king through him, and how should that be represented without changing the selected subject?
